| [NOTE-330](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-330.md) | Damasio & Carvalho — The nature of feelings | An Opinion with no new data. It needs the upper brainstem, where whole-body maps first assemble. | [NOTE-1102](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1102.md) | Control Theory, Goal Attainment, and Psychopathology | A commentary. | [NOTE-1108](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1108.md) | Levels of valence | A framework, not a study. Valence is located at two levels. | [NOTE-1110](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1110.md) | Berridge and Kringelbach — Pleasure systems in the brain | A review. Reward splits into 'liking', 'wanting' and learning. | [NOTE-1111](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1111.md) | Hesp et al. — Deeply felt affect: the emergence of valence in deep active inference | A computational proof of principle with no data. | [NOTE-1114](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1114.md) | Motivational trade-offs and modulation of nociception in bumblebees | A motivational trade-off in an insect. | [NOTE-1115](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1115.md) | Conscious emotional experience emerges as a function of multilevel, appraisal-driven response synchronization | A theoretical paper with a short review of EEG and neural-synchrony evidence. | [NOTE-1117](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1117.md) | The power of goal-directed processes in the causation of emotional and other actions | A reversal of the default in dual-process models of action and emotion. Emotional actions are those whose tendencies have control precedence because the goals at stake are highly valued, so emotional episodes are decision processes with higher stakes. | Read |
| [NOTE-1118](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1118.md) | A Multi-Componential Approach to Emotion Recognition and the Effect of Personality | A crowdsourced film-rating study. Thirty-nine CoreGRID items rated after whole clips show emotion structure beyond valence and arousal (six dimensions) and predict discrete-emotion ratings better together than any component alone. Personality traits correlate with componential items. No synchronization, no within-episode measure, no physiology recorded. | Read |
| [NOTE-1119](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1119.md) | Bridging emotion theory and neurobiology through dynamic systems modeling | A dynamic-systems model of appraisal and emotion. Their constituents organize one another through feedback and circular causality into one emotional interpretation (EI): triggered by a perturbation, self-amplifying until it takes over the system, then self-stabilizing as competing cues are resolved. EIs are attractors, one at a time, with abrupt transitions between them. Vertical integration gives them momentum and selects among them. Stable EIs drive learning, so real-time and developmental order are interdependent. Predicts theta-band phase synchrony as an index of emotional relevance. | Read |
| [NOTE-1120](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1120.md) | Brown, Price & Dombrovski — Anxiety as a disorder of uncertainty | A narrative review and theoretical proposal, with no new data and no simulation. Computational learning studies of anxiety (seven, not a systematic search) find altered adjustment of learning rate to kinds of uncertainty, mostly with aversive outcomes, rather than inflated threat learning or valuation. The authors propose that in aversive environments avoidance of uncertain states keeps their uncertainty high and so perpetuates itself, that anxiety amplifies this by misreading noise as change, and that exposure works by reducing the uncertainty, not the threat. It covers fear-based disorders and says it does not explain GAD. | Read |
| [NOTE-1127](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1127.md) | Chou, Wilson & Smith — The influence of anxiety on exploration | A narrative review of computational modelling studies of anxiety and exploration, almost all in reward tasks and sub-clinical samples. In bandit tasks, directed exploration tends to rise with trait or cognitive anxiety and fall with state or somatic anxiety; random exploration shows no link; in foraging tasks, and in one task with a predator to check for, anxiety goes with less exploration. Results are inconsistent across tasks and measures and none has been replicated. | Read |
| [NOTE-1133](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1133.md) | Ku & Finch — Routines die hard: ontological agency in securitisation | A conceptual paper with an illustration. Alongside the political agency securitisation theory grants its audience (accept, reject, contest), Ku and Finch propose ontological agency: keeping everyday routines going, which often means ignoring securitising moves. Observed by chance in Gangneung in 2022, people paid routine missile launches and beach-front military sites little attention; when a missile malfunctioned at night under a news embargo, tweets voiced fear of war and anger at the government. The authors argue such inaction lets securitisation reproduce itself and that accepting it delegates anxiety management to elites. | Read |
